post.title: Save $100 in a 401(k), take-home drops $78? Here's why
post.ig:
Squirrel saves $100. His paycheck only shrinks $78.

A traditional 401(k) takes money out before federal income tax (IRS).
Example, 22% federal bracket in 2026: $100 in, $22 less income tax, take-home down $78. Social Security and Medicare (7.65%) still apply.
Over 26 paychecks: $2,600 in, take-home down $2,028 (example; ignores state tax).
The tax is delayed, not skipped: withdrawals are taxed as income, and before age 59 1/2 there's usually an extra 10% tax unless an exception applies.

Sources: IRS 401(k) Plan Overview; IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32; IRS Topic 558; SSA (2026).
